21874-the-bay-and-padie-book.title: Kiddie Songs
21874-the-bay-and-padie-book.creator: Furnley Maurice
21874-the-bay-and-padie-book.description: A book by Furnley Maurice. My mother and my father are both having tea to drink;   Inside the pastry shop they saw me last. They don't know where I've got to, for I've runned from where they think;   I heard the soldier band go marching past.

arxiv-1912-07391.title: Model reduction for linear parameter-varying systems through parameter projection
arxiv-1912-07391.creator: Sil Schouten, Daming Lou, Siep Weiland
arxiv-1912-07391.description: Abstract For affine linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems, this paper develops two parameter reduction methods for reducing the dimension of the parameter space. The first method achieves the complexity reduction by transforming the affine LPV system into a parameter-ordered form and establishing an affine upper bound of the system Gramians, which is extended to time-varying rate-bounded parameters.

arxiv-2206-11146.title: Modeling Emergent Lexicon Formation with a Self-Reinforcing Stochastic Process
arxiv-2206-11146.creator: Brendon Boldt, David Mortensen
arxiv-2206-11146.description: Abstract We introduce FiLex , a self-reinforcing stochastic process which models finite lexicons in emergent language experiments. The central property of FiLex is that it is a self-reinforcing process, parallel to the intuition that the more a word is used in a language, the more its use will continue.

arxiv-2208-00393.title: Significance of the nature of disorder on the universal features of the spatio-temporal correlations of two-dimensional Coulomb-clusters
arxiv-2208-00393.creator: Jami Prashanti, Biswarup Ash, Amit Ghosal
arxiv-2208-00393.description: Abstract We comprehend the role of imperfections in materials consisting of interacting particles, arising from different origins on their universal features. Specifically, we report the static and dynamic responses in a cluster of Coulomb interacting particles in two dimensions. Confined systems with pinned impurities are studied, and results are compared with those from irregularly trapped system of particles.

arxiv-2301-09826.title: The Geometry of Rank Drop in a Class of Face-Splitting Matrix Products: Part I
arxiv-2301-09826.creator: Erin Connelly, Sameer Agarwal, Alperen Ergur, Rekha R. Thomas
arxiv-2301-09826.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Erin Connelly, Sameer Agarwal, Alperen Ergur, Rekha R. Thomas. Given k k points ( x i , y i ) ∈ ℙ 2 × ℙ 2 (x_{i},y_{i})\in\mathbb{P}^{2}\times\mathbb{P}^{2} , we characterize rank deficiency of the k × 9 k\times 9 matrix Z k Z_{k} with rows x i ⊤ ⊗ y i ⊤ x_{i}^{\top}\otimes y_{i}^{\top} in terms of the geometry of the point configurations { x i } \{x_{i}\} and { y i } \{y_{i}\} .

arxiv-2304-00998.title: Forward and inverse problems for subdiffusion equation with time-dependent coefficients
arxiv-2304-00998.creator: Ravshan Ashurov, Yusuf Fayziev, Muattar Khudoykulova
arxiv-2304-00998.description: Abstract . In this paper, we consider forward and inverse problems for subdiffusion equations with time-dependent coefficients. The fractional derivative is taken in the sense of Riemann-Liouville. Using the classical Fourier method, the theorem of the uniqueness and existence of forward and inverse problems for determining the right-hand side of the equation are proved.

arxiv-2312-10842.title: Compositional Inductive Invariant Based Verification of Neural Network Controlled Systems
arxiv-2312-10842.creator: Yuhao Zhou, Stavros Tripakis
arxiv-2312-10842.description: Abstract The integration of neural networks into safety-critical systems has shown great potential in recent years. However, the challenge of effectively verifying the safety of Neural Network Controlled Systems (NNCS) persists. This paper introduces a novel approach to NNCS safety verification, leveraging the inductive invariant method.

arxiv-2404-02689.title: Social clustering reinforces external influence on the majority opinion model Journal: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
arxiv-2404-02689.creator: Niels Van Santen, Jan Ryckebusch, Luis E. C. Rocha
arxiv-2404-02689.description: Abstract Public opinion is subject to peer interaction via social networks and external pressure from the media, advertising, and other actors. In this paper, we study the interaction between external and peer influence on the stochastic opinion dynamics of a majority vote model.

arxiv-2410-01579.title: Spoken Grammar Assessment Using LLM
arxiv-2410-01579.creator: Sunil Kumar Kopparapu, Chitralekha Bhat, Ashish Panda, Sunil Kumar Kopparapu, Chitralekha Bhat, Ashish Panda
arxiv-2410-01579.description: Abstract Spoken language assessment (SLA) systems restrict themselves to evaluating the pronunciation and oral fluency of a speaker by analysing the read and spontaneous spoken utterances respectively. The assessment of language grammar or vocabulary is relegated to written language assessment (WLA) systems.

arxiv-2410-04983.title: RoWeeder: Unsupervised Weed Mapping through Crop-Row Detection
arxiv-2410-04983.creator: Pasquale De Marinis, Gennaro Vessio, Giovanna Castellano
arxiv-2410-04983.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Pasquale De Marinis, Gennaro Vessio, Giovanna Castellano. Precision agriculture relies heavily on effective weed management to ensure robust crop yields. This study presents RoWeeder, an innovative framework for unsupervised weed mapping that combines crop-row detection with a noise-resilient deep learning model. By leveraging crop-row information to create a pseudo-ground truth, our method trains a lightweight deep learning model capable of distinguishing between crops and weeds, even in the presence of noisy data.

arxiv-2506-19220.title: Private Model Personalization Revisited
arxiv-2506-19220.creator: Conor Snedeker Xinyu Zhou Raef Bassily
arxiv-2506-19220.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Conor Snedeker Xinyu Zhou Raef Bassily. We study model personalization under user-level differential privacy (DP) in the shared representation framework. In this problem, there are n n users whose data is statistically heterogeneous, and their optimal parameters share an unknown embedding U ∗ ∈ ℝ d × k U^{*}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times k} that maps the user parameters in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} to low-dimensional representations in ℝ k \mathbb{R}^{k} , where k ≪ d k\ll d .

arxiv-2507-00201.title: Probing the variations of interstellar dust abundance and properties within and between galaxies with HWO UV spectroscopy in the Local Volume
arxiv-2507-00201.creator: Roman-Duval, Julia, 1 Boquien, Mederic, 2 and Choi, Yumi 3, Endorsed by: Michelle Berg (Texas Christian University), Emanuele Bertone (Instituto Nacional de Astrófisica, Óptica y Electrónica, Mexico), Christopher Clark (AURA for the European Space Agency/Space Telescope Science Institute), Melanie C
arxiv-2507-00201.description: Abstract The cycle of metals between the gas and the dust phases in the neutral interstellar medium (ISM) is an integral part of the baryon cycle in galaxies. The resulting variations in the abundance and properties of interstellar dust have important implications for how accurately we can trace the chemical enrichment of the universe over cosmic time.

arxiv-2512-08540.title: Tunable passive squeezing of squeezed light through unbalanced double homodyne detection Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2512-08540.creator: Niels Tripier-Mondancin 1, David Barral 1,2,*, Ganaël Roeland 1, Raúl Leonardo Rincon Celis 1, Yann Bouchereau 1, Nicolas Treps 1
arxiv-2512-08540.description: Abstract The full characterization of quantum states of light is a central task in quantum optics and information science. Double homodyne detection provides a powerful method for the direct measurement of the Husimi Q quasi-probability distribution, offering a complete state representation in a simple experimental setting and a limited time frame.

pmc-10626753.title: Addition of aspirin to venous thromboembolism chemoprophylaxis safely decreases venous thromboembolism rates in trauma patients
pmc-10626753.creator: Daniel Lammers, Michelle Scerbo, Annamaria Davidson, Matthew Pommerening, Jeffrey Tomasek, Charles E Wade, Jessica Cardenas, Jan Jansen, Charles C Miller, John B Holcomb
pmc-10626753.description: BackgroundTrauma patients exhibit a multifactorial hypercoagulable state and have increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Despite early and aggressive chemoprophylaxis (CP) with various heparin compounds (“standard” CP; sCP), VTE rates remain high. In high-quality studies, aspirin has been shown to decrease VTE in postoperative elective surgical and orthopedic trauma patients.

pmc-10683929.title: Relationship of Main Pulmonary Artery (Truncus Pulmonalis) Diameter With Hospital Stay and Mortality in Pulmonary Hypertension Patients Admitted to the Emergency Department
pmc-10683929.creator: Mehmet Cagrı Goktekin, Feyza Aksu, Ahmet Zafer Perilioglu, Ramazan Fazil Akkoc
pmc-10683929.description: Introduction: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a haemodynamic and pathophysiological disease significantly associated with morbidity and mortality. The increase in pulmonary vascular resistance, high pulmonary artery pressure and wall tension that occurs in PH results in dilatation of the main pulmonary artery (truncus pulmonalis), one of the largest and most important vessels in the body.

pmc-11557414.title: Exploring the mechanism of tetramethylpyrazine in the treatment of osteoarthritis based on network pharmacology
pmc-11557414.creator: Juncen Li, Daiying Song, Bohui Li, Yajie Wang, Huilin Sun, Qinglin Li, Xiangming Lin, Di Wang, Guangdong Zhou, Yu Liu
pmc-11557414.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundOsteoarthritis (OA) is the most common joint disease, which mainly damages articular cartilage and involves the whole joint tissue. It has the characteristics of long course, repeated symptoms and high disability rate, and the incidence trend is gradually increasing.

pmc-11600617.title: Analysis of vaginal microbiota during postpartum and postmenopausal periods based on metagenomics
pmc-11600617.creator: Xiaocui Li, Zhan Zhang, Huihui Bai, Zhaohui Liu
pmc-11600617.description: BackgroundPostmenopausal and the postpartum periods are essential physiological phases that result in low estrogen levels in women; however, they are important to female reproductive health. Traditional as well as new detection methods (such as 16 S RNA sequencing) have limitations in detecting the composition of vaginal microbiota.

pmc-12609208.title: Transmit–Receive Module Diagnostic of Active Phased Array Antenna Using Side-Lobe Blanking Channel
pmc-12609208.creator: Hongwoo Park, Wonjin Lee, Hyun Seok Oh, Seunghee Seo, Shin Young Cho, Hongjoon Kim, Yuan Yao, Jia-Lin Kang
pmc-12609208.description: This article presents a diagnostic method for transmit–receive modules (TRMs) in an airborne active phased array antenna (APAA). Given the spatial constraints of airborne radar systems, the diagnostic functionality was implemented using the peripheral probe method. To minimize the space, cost, and time required for modifications to the existing APAA, the side-lobe blanking (SLB) channel was employed as the probe.

pmc-12628876.title: A qualitative evaluation of older people’s perceptions towards optimal diet management in the context of antimicrobial resistance
pmc-12628876.creator: Lorna Flintham, Charlotte Dack, Francoise Koumanov, Edward Feil, Ben Ainsworth
pmc-12628876.description: IntroductionAntimicrobial Resistance (AMR) poses a significant global public health problem. The risk of developing a reservoir of antimicrobial resistant genes in the gut is reportedly higher with certain diets, rendering individual diet-related AMR management a largely untapped approach in AMR mitigation. As a vulnerable population, older people are at particular risk of poorer resistant infection outcomes.

pmc-13180795.title: Type 2 Diabetes, Glycemic Traits and Overall Cancer Risk: A Large‐Scale Prospective Cohort Study
pmc-13180795.creator: Aiping Zhang, Xia Zhu, Zhe Li, Yaoyao Li, Meng Zhu, Caiwang Yan, Guangfu Jin, Pengpeng Cai, Min Zhang, Yanbing Ding
pmc-13180795.description: BackgroundEvidence concerning the associations of T2D and glycemic traits with overall cancer risk and their combined effect with genetic susceptibility remains inconsistent and unexplored.MethodsThis large‐scale prospective cohort study included 475,637 eligible participants from the UK Biobank. We identified 25,887 participants with T2D by clinical data, baseline self‐report data, and biochemistry data. HbA1c and random blood glucose were measured at baseline.

pmc-13282594.title: Health Care Use and Recurrence Rate in Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn: Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13282594.creator: Nehaa Khadka, Michael J Fassett, Carol Mao, Fagen Xie, Vicki Y Chiu, Jiaxiao M Shi, Theresa M Im, Sunhea Kim, Daniella Park, Darios Getahun, Matthew Balcarras, Morgan R Peltier, Zainab Lawal, Supriya Bisht, Atefeh Shamsi
pmc-13282594.description: BackgroundHemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) is a life-threatening condition resulting from maternal-fetal erythrocyte antigen incompatibility. Although anti–Rhesus D (RhD) prophylaxis has reduced RhD-associated cases, HDFN persists due to non-RhD antibodies and gaps in prevention. Population-based data on maternal and neonatal outcomes and recurrence patterns are limited.

pmc-13457244.title: Five-year outcomes of the PROVE-IT randomized controlled trial: Patient-Reported Outcomes of Robotic vs. Laparoscopic Ventral Hernia Repair with Intraperitoneal Mesh
pmc-13457244.creator: Erika M Schmidt, William C Bennett, Noah X Tocci, Alvaro C Carvalho, Cammy Tang, Chao Tu, Kimberly S Miles, Luciano Tastaldi, Benjamin T Miller, Lucas R Beffa, David M Krpata, Clayton C Petro, Ajita S Prabhu
pmc-13457244.description: BackgroundThe Patient-Reported Outcomes of Robotic vs. Laparoscopic Ventral Hernia Repair with Intraperitoneal Mesh (PROVE-IT) randomized controlled trial previously demonstrated comparable pain at 1 year postoperatively between laparoscopic (lapIPOM) and robotic (rIPOM) approaches, although with potential differences in quality of life and recurrence. We aim to report 5-year follow-up of the PROVE-IT trial.
